To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the system is more reliable and cost-effective if the standby unit fails due to power fluctuations rather than operator's inefficiency and vice versa for the operative unit.
the cost of the system is a function of the cost of the standby unit, the cost of the operative unit, the cost to interchange (of the two units) and the cost of the repair of both the units.

the system's reliability characteristics, such as the expected number of failures and the expected number of repairs, are dependent on the failure and repair rates of the operative unit, the failure and repair rate of the standby unit, and the failure rate of the power supply, the cost of repair of the standby and operative units, the cost of interchange of units, and the time to interchange.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) The system is chargeable, i.e. it has to be charged after a fixed time of operation; (ii) The system can fail due to power fluctuations and operator inefficiency; (iii) The units are interchangeable; (iv) The failure time distribution is exponential while the repair time distribution is general; (v) The cost of the system and its components are considered.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system with interchangeable units performs better than that without interchangeable units.
, for the model considered, the system with interchangeable units is more reliable and more economical than the system without interchangeable units.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cost analysis of a two unit chargeable standby system is more complex compared to a single unit system and is dependent on the type of failure, the cost of the standby unit, the repair time and interchange time distributions.
the cost-benefit of such a system depends on the relative cost of the two types of failures and on the cost of interchange of the two units.
the cost of a two-unit system with interchangeable units is less than that of a two-unit noninterchangeable system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system's reliability is improved with the introduction of the interchange facility.
, for the given system configuration, the optimal number of units to be purchased and their optimal cost is obtained by minimizing the expected cost rate.
the system with interchangeable units is better than that without interchangeability, and the system with a single type of failure is better than the system with two types of failure.
